# JMIR: Factors influencing admission decisions in SNFs

- Citation: Strickland et al., "Factors Influencing Admission Decisions in Skilled Nursing Facilities: Retrospective Quantitative Study." J Med Internet Res 2023. https://www.jmir.org/2023/1/e43518 (PubMed 37195755)
- Year: 2023
- Tier: 1 (peer-reviewed)
- Sample / method: retrospective analysis of referral data from 627 SNFs, Jan 2020 to Mar 2022, from a health informatics database; regression of accept/deny on daily operations (occupancy, nursing hours), referral factors (insurance, primary diagnosis) and facility factors (star rating, urban/rural).
- Key findings: diagnosis and payer type were the strongest drivers of acceptance. Acceptance fell 67.0% for Medicaid and 21.6% for managed care, and rose 13.7% for private insurance. No significant link between occupancy or nursing hours and acceptance. Urban SNFs accepted less often than rural ones.
- Limits: findings come from the search-result abstract summary; the full text wasn't read (the PMC fetch failed). The data provider wasn't confirmed. The period spans COVID.
- Relevance: declines are driven by payer and clinical fit, not only response speed. This qualifies a speed-first framing.
